title: Did Rizal want the Philippines to become a province of Spain?
big_number_label: the year the Philippines lost its representatives in the Cortes, Spain's parliament
takeaways: One of the goals of the Propaganda Movement, Rizal included, was assimilation: making the Philippines a full province of Spain so Filipinos would have the same rights as Spaniards.
They also asked for representation in the Cortes again, freedom of the press, and equal treatment under the law. They fought for it in their newspaper, La Solidaridad.
It was not a rejection of being Filipino. In his essay Filipinas dentro de cien años, Rizal even warned that the Philippines could break away if Spain refused to listen.

quiz.q: What was the proposal to make the Philippines a province of Spain called?
What was the name of the reformists' newspaper, founded in Barcelona in 1889?

paragraphs: Did you know that José Rizal wanted the Philippines to become a province of Spain? Yes, you heard that right! But why would he want us to be under Spain? Didn't he fight for Filipinos? In the 19th century, the Philippines was under Spanish rule. But Filipinos and Spaniards were not treated equally. Many Filipinos lacked basic rights and had no voice in government. And did you know? The Philippines once had representatives in the Cortes, Spain's parliament. But in 1837, they were removed. So Filipinos no longer had a voice in Madrid.

So Rizal, together with other Filipino reformists in Spain, like Marcelo H. del Pilar and Mariano Ponce, called for reform. One of their most important proposals? What is called assimilation: making the Philippines a full province of Spain, so that Filipinos would have the same rights as Spaniards. This included having representatives in the Cortes again, freedom of the press, and equal treatment under the law. They fought for it in their own newspaper, La Solidaridad. Their weapon was the pen, not arms.

But wait! This doesn't mean Rizal wanted Filipinos to lose their identity. What he wanted was equal rights, dignity, and recognition of Filipinos as citizens who should not be treated as inferior. That is why, in his novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo, he exposed the abuses in the colony. And here's more! In his essay Filipinas dentro de cien años, Rizal warned that if Spain kept ignoring Filipinos, the day might come when the Philippines would break away. So yes, making the Philippines a province of Spain was part of Rizal's earlier aims. But the bigger question is: if Spain had granted their reforms, would our country's history have been different?
